item.title: Cytotoxic CD4<sup>+</sup> T cells support age-associated myelopoiesis
item.content:encoded: Aging is associated with myeloid-biased hematopoiesis, which leads to the establishment of a pro-inflammatory microenvironment. We discovered that cytotoxic CD4+ T cells foster this process via the CCL5–CCR5 axis and found that the clinically approved CCR5 antagonist maraviroc can rebalance immunity in aged mice.

item.title: Everything you need to know about bird flu - Benjamin Anderson
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Dig into the science of avian influenza to find out what makes the H5N1 virus so dangerous, and its potential to jump to humans.
--
While avian influenza used to infect mostly birds, in the past few years, it’s been found in over 70 mammal species, including cats, dairy cows, foxes, seals, and bears. Each new mammalian infection gives the virus more chances to drift or shift, spill over into humans, and ignite a pandemic. So, what is it about H5N1 that makes it so frighteningly flexible? Benjamin Anderson investigates.
Lesson by Benjamin Anderson, directed by Anton Bogaty.

item.title: A microprotein atlas of the human frontal cortex in Alzheimer’s disease
item.author: Alan Saghatelian
item.content:encoded: A new atlas identifies 1,067 unannotated microproteins in the human frontal cortex with strong spectral grades. A subset is differentially expressed in Alzheimer’s disease independently of their canonical genes, including an MKKS-derived microprotein required for normal microglial mitochondrial respiration.

item.title: Large-scale mapping of microproteins in the aged human brain
item.content:encoded: Microproteins, small proteins of 100–150 amino acids, are largely absent from reference proteomes and have been overlooked in brain and aging research. An atlas of the aged human brain catalogs over 1,000 high-confidence microproteins, including one encoded by the MKKS gene that is reduced in Alzheimer’s disease and regulates energy production in microglia.

item.title: Fibronectin mediates APOE4-driven blood–brain barrier dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease
item.author: Caghan Kizil
item.content:encoded: Bhattarai, Yilmaz and colleagues identify astrocyte-derived fibronectin as a key driver of blood–brain barrier dysfunction in Alzheimer’s disease, linking APOE ε4 and amyloid pathology to vascular damage and highlighting FN1 as a potential therapeutic target.

item.title: Why do some people have a better sense of direction than others? - Oliver Baumann
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Dig into the neuroscience behind our sense of direction and find out why some people are better at navigating than others.
--
Whether you identify as a wayfinding whiz or get lost returning from the grocery store, your brain has a built-in navigation system that facilitates spatial skills, from sensing which direction is north to map-reading and route-learning. So, why do we still struggle to find our way? And why do some of us find ourselves lost more often than others? Oliver Baumann digs into our sense of direction.
Lesson by Oliver Baumann, directed by Anton Bogaty.

item.title: Ever walk into a room and forget what you were doing? - Gabriel Radvansky
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Dig into the phenomenon known as the doorway effect, where walking into a new space can make you forget what you were doing.
--
You enter your living room, then pause. Uh-oh, what was it that you were doing? You feel your mission’s momentum wane, and its aim is suddenly lost. So, what just happened? Well, you’re not alone; this is a common memory lapse phenomenon scientists have termed the “doorway effect.” Gabriel Radvansky explores why walking into a new space can make you suddenly forget what you were doing.

item.title: What are tariffs, and how do they work?
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Explore how tariffs work and dig into how their enactment can set off an economic chain reaction that impacts global trade.
--
In 1930, in hopes of supporting farms and manufacturing, President Hoover made a bold decision: he approved a sweeping 20% tax on all imported agricultural and industrial goods. But the plan completely backfired, leading exports to fall and global trade to decline. And it wouldn't be the last time a world leader was shocked by a tariff’s consequences. Trace the economic chain reaction of tariffs.
Directed by Avi Ofer.

item.title: Plato’s infamous Ship of State thought experiment - Michael Vazquez
item.author: TED-Ed
item.content:encoded:
Dig into Plato’s infamous Ship of State thought experiment, which explores how democratic societies handle leadership and power.
--
Imagine a ship struggling in an endless storm. Its captain, though strong and commanding, is a terrible navigator. Neither he nor his crew have been trained to sail, yet they tirelessly vie for control through bribery, flattery, and mutiny, and ignore those with real navigation knowledge. This dysfunctional vessel is Plato's Ship of State. Michael Vazquez explores the infamous thought experiment.
Lesson by Michael Vazquez, directed by Luis Torres, Mr. Flama.
This video was produced in collaboration with the Parr Center for Ethics, housed within the renowned Philosophy Department at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. The Parr Center is committed to integrating abstract work in ethical theory with the informed discussion of practical ethical issues, and prides itself on the development of innovative and inclusive approaches to moral and civic education.

item.content:encoded: В Первую Мировую солдаты бежали с фронта, сдавались в плен, калечили себя, терялись при переходах, братались с противником. В ответ на это офицеры расстреливали и пороли подчинённых, и чем дольше шла война, тем больше армия теряла дисциплину. Посреди всего этого артиллерист Михаил Анисимов заряжает пушку и молится БогуПодписывайтесь на соцсети:Выпуск вместе со мной готовили:Оськин М.В Неизвестные трагедии первой мировой. Пленные. item.title: Биолог МГУ: «Грибы — ГЛАВНАЯ угроза человечеству». Михаил Вишневский
item.content:encoded: В новом выпуске — разговор с Михаилом Вишневским, кандидатом биологических наук, военным врачом, микологом и автором более двух десятков книг, который много лет изучает грибы, их эволюцию и влияние на человека. Мы обсудили, почему патогенные грибы становятся всё опаснее, как они приобретают устойчивость к лекарствам, могут ли они вызвать глобальный голод и почему некоторые из них, наоборот, способны помогать человеку.— Почему грибы ежегодно убивают миллионы людей и почему их опасность растёт?— Почему современные патогенные грибы всё чаще поражают даже здоровых людей?— Как сельское хозяйство и массовое использование фунгицидов сделали грибы устойчивыми к лекарствам?— Насколько опасна плесень в квартире и почему микотоксины невозможно просто уничтожить?— Могут ли грибы уничтожить урожай и привести человечество к новому глобальному голоду?— Правда ли, что существует гриб, способный разрушать пластик?— Может ли грибковая инфекция стать угрозой для всей человеческой цивилизации?— Действительно ли ежовик гребенчатый способен восстанавливать нервную ткань и улучшать нейропластичность?— Почему псилоцибиновые грибы могли повлиять на развитие человеческого сознания и религии?

item.title: Your Inner Cosmos with David Eagleman
item.author: Neil deGrasse Tyson, Chuck Nice, Gary O'Reilly, David Eagleman
item.content:encoded: What are the limits of the human mind? Neil deGrasse Tyson, Chuck Nice, and Gary O’Reilly explore sensory perception, dreaming, synesthesia, time, and the flexibility of the human brain with neuroscientist David Eagleman.
